name: Xberg
tagline: Polyglot document intelligence: text, tables, and code from 106 formats
seoTitle: Xberg: Fast Document Text Extraction Engine
metaDescription: Xberg is a Rust-core document intelligence engine that extracts text, tables, metadata, and structured data from 106 file formats with OCR, no GPU needed.
overview: Xberg is an open-source document intelligence engine built on a Rust core. The project describes itself as the next iteration of Kreuzberg — the same engine, rebuilt and rebranded under a fresh v1 line. Point it at a PDF, a spreadsheet, a scanned image, an audio file, a URL, an archive, or a source tree and it returns clean text, tables, metadata, and structured data.

One core handles format detection, reading, OCR, and extraction, so you do not assemble a pipeline from a dozen libraries. It covers 106 document formats across 140 file extensions, adds code intelligence for 371 programming languages, and emits six output formats: plain text, Markdown, Djot, HTML, a JSON tree, or Docling DocTags.

The same engine is callable from 15 language bindings — Rust, Python, Node.js, Go, Java, C#, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, Dart, Swift, Zig, WASM, Kotlin, and C FFI — and runs as a library, a CLI, a REST API (`xberg serve`), an MCP server, a Docker image, or a Helm chart. It is MIT-licensed and runs on CPU by default, with no GPU required.
features: Reads 106 document formats across 140 file extensions, with MIME detection and bounded extraction controls
OCR on demand through Tesseract, PaddleOCR, Candle, or VLM backends, with fallback chains and confidence scores
ML layout models and table-structure models reconstruct reading order and cell grids for clean Markdown
Code intelligence for 371 programming languages: functions, classes, imports, symbols, docstrings, and syntax-aware chunking
Recursive archive traversal (.zip, .tar, .gz, .7z) guarded by zip-bomb, compression-ratio, and nesting-depth limits
Optional URL ingestion and crawling, audio/video transcription via Whisper ONNX, embeddings, and reranking
15 language bindings plus library, CLI, REST API, MCP server, Docker, and Helm deployment modes

gettingStarted.intro: Xberg ships prebuilt language packages that bundle the common feature set. Pick the binding that matches your stack, or run the container to use it as a service.

steps.heading: Install for Python
steps.body: The PyPI package wraps the Rust core with the common features prebuilt.

steps.heading: Install for Node.js
steps.body: The Node.js package is published under the xberg-io scope; a WASM build is also available as @xberg-io/xberg-wasm.

steps.heading: Add to a Rust project
steps.body: Use the core crate directly for feature-flag control over URL ingestion, transcription, reranking, and layout models.

steps.heading: Run it as a service
steps.body: The container image on GitHub Container Registry runs the CLI, the REST API, or the MCP server without installing a language binding. A Helm chart is documented for Kubernetes.

useCases: Building a RAG pipeline that needs clean text and metadata from mixed document types such as PDFs, Office files, and emails
Running OCR on scanned PDFs and images to recover searchable text without setting up a GPU
Indexing source code repositories by extracting functions, classes, and imports across hundreds of programming languages
Exposing a shared extraction service to many apps through the REST API or MCP server, callable from 15 languages
